text:
sre-oncall: alert: multiple node groups in europe-west1 are reporting UNREACHABLE and API 5xx spikes, high error budget burn :rotating_light:
incidents-bot: Incident created: #EW1-REGION-OUTAGE (sev=page) by monitoring@sre - alerts: node_unreachable, lb_5xx_rate, vpc_peer_down
cloud-status-bot: Provider status: https://status.cloudvendor.example/incidents/ew1 - degraded networking in europe-west1 (investigating)
ashley: oncall here, I'm pulling node logs and control plane metrics. Starting with `kubectl get nodes -o wide --selector=region=europe-west1`
mike: seeing heavy RTOs to the model-serving pods, KV cache miss rates spiking. Throughput down ~70% for ew1 traffic
kevin: netops confirms multiple VPC routes flapping between our peering and provider backbone in ew1. Likely upstream routing blackhole. I'm opening a ticket with cloud vendor NOC now: INC-98721
danya: product impact — some Dedicated customers in EU reporting 504s. Notifying CS to open incidents to affected accounts. Keeping them updated with expected mitigation steps
ashley: quick triage notes: `kubectl get pods --namespace=model-serving -l region=europe-west1` shows many pods Pending or CrashLoopBackOff with `dial tcp: i/o timeout` in logs
mike: trying graceful fallback: switching traffic for the heaviest routes to europe-west2 via smart-routing — initiating policy: `route-policy shift ew1->ew2 50% 5m`
sre-oncall: initiating emergency routing override to 100% for critical routes only. Will keep non-critical traffic queued. Executing `redwoodctl traffic shift --from=ew1 --to=ew2 --scope=critical --now`
kevin: provider NOC says they're seeing BGP flap between two backbone POPs in ew1 and are rolling filters. ETA unclear ("under 2 hours" but no guarantees).
ashley: starting graceful pod evacuation for stateful workers in ew1 to avoid split kv-store writes. Command: ```
kubectl cordon node-14-ew1
kubectl drain node-14-ew1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
mike: enabling model-fallbacks on the serving plane to smaller quantized variants to reduce resource pressure in ew2 while we shift traffic: `modelset rollout --fallback-profile=lowmem-quant`
danya: CS: customers with Dedicated contracts get proactive outreach. I've drafted a short blurb: "We're experiencing a regional networking outage in europe-west1; we're failing over to adjacent regions and expect progressive recovery. We'll update in 30m." Approving? :thumbsup:
kevin: adding temporary BGP community to prefer ew2 in our transit: `transitctl set-preference --region=ew2 --community=65200:10`
sre-oncall: mitigation checklist update: 1) provider NOC engaged 2) traffic shifted for critical routes -> ew2 3) cordon/drain in-progress 4) fallback models enabled 5) customer comms sent 6) exec pager if >1h
ashley: observed KV replication lag for persistent caches — pausing writes to non-critical namespaces to avoid cascading failures. Patch: `redis-cli -h redis-ew1 --eval "REPLICAOF NO ONE"` (manual step will be reverted after recovery)
mike: perf note: ew2 node pools at 85% GPU utilization after shift. Might need burst capacity or autoscale. Filing request to infra-provisioner for emergency spare nodes in eu: PR-4531
kevin: NOC updated: "partial stabilization detected, some peering paths restored but intermittent. Continue failover until confirmed stable."
incidents-bot: Updated incident status: mitigation in progress. Next update scheduled in 15 minutes.
sre-oncall: raising to SEV1 if vendor ETA slips past 1h. For now keeping page and oncall rotation intact. Leaving this thread open for updates.
